title: Water at 750 Degrees That Never Boils (1.5 Miles Under the Sea)

scenes.text: There's water at 750 degrees that never boils.
scenes.keywords: black smoker hydrothermal vent deep sea

scenes.text: A mile and a half down, chimneys on the sea floor blast out black water hot enough to melt lead.
400 degrees Celsius. On the surface, water boils at 100.
Down here, the pressure is 250 times the surface. Water can't turn to steam.
Two feet away, the sea is two degrees. In between live tube worms six feet long.
Nobody knew it existed until 1977. 750 degrees. Never boils.

description:
Black smoker hydrothermal vents on the deep sea floor spew mineral-rich water at around 400 degrees Celsius, about 750 Fahrenheit, yet it never boils.
At depths of 2,500 metres the pressure is roughly 250 times that at the surface, far too high for steam to form. The first vents were discovered in 1977 by the submersible Alvin near the Galapagos, surrounded by giant tube worms and clams living without sunlight.
Would you ride in a submersible to see one? Comment below.
first_comment: Some black smoker chimneys grow 180 feet tall. The tube worms have no mouth or gut; bacteria inside them turn vent chemicals into food. What would you name a vent creature?
